metadata.title: Flagward Telemetry — how Flagward is used
metadata.description: Public, aggregate and anonymous usage statistics from self-hosted Flagward installations.

hero.title: How Flagward is used
hero.subtitle: Every self-hosted Flagward sends one anonymous heartbeat a day. These are the aggregates — the same numbers anyone can fetch as JSON.

headline.newUnconfirmed: New this week, not yet confirmed
headline.newUnconfirmedHint: Sent on a single day so far. Counted once they report on a second day.
headline.establishedHint: Installations that reported on at least two different days.

sdks.title: SDK adoption
sdks.hint: Share of installations with at least one environment using each SDK in the last 7 days.
sdks.empty: No SDK has reached five installations yet.

features.title: Feature adoption
features.rollout: Roll out a variant to a segment

notEnough.title: Not enough data yet
notEnough.body: Breakdowns appear once at least five installations have reported on two different days, so no single installation can be singled out.

privacy.title: What we collect, and what we never do
privacy.collected: Counts, versions and on/off settings — never names, emails, flag keys, API keys or hostnames.
privacy.ip: IP addresses are never stored: our proxy drops them before the request reaches this service, and keeps no access logs.
privacy.groups: Groups smaller than five installations are shown as “Other”, and each installation counts once, however large it is.
privacy.disableBody: Set this in your Flagward environment and restart:

footer.tagline: Anonymous usage statistics for Flagward, the open-source feature flag platform.
